speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Government can provide an update on the recent period of home-based learning (HBL) that is implemented in late September/early October 2021 for primary school students in terms of the impact on their learning and development; and (b) whether this indicates a possible shift to more HBL periods for schools in the future.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: asked the Minister for Education whether the Ministry will consider moving schools to HBL in view of the spike in the number of COVID-19 cases.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It also imposes a burden on families and society.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Moreover, not all students have a home environment conducive to HBL.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The past few months have given us greater confidence that we can strike a balance by taking a more targeted approach to ringfence cases and their close contacts.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For example, rather than resorting to full HBL across all schools, or the entire level, we would only place affected classes on HBL in response to a confirmed case, if there is a possibility of transmission within schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Schools mitigate the impact of HBL by using technology to minimise disruption to curriculum coverage and maintain social connections.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Teachers use online platforms and resources to ensure that students who are away from school can continue learning and conduct regular check-ins with these students to monitor their well-being.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Schools have sufficient computing devices and Internet-enabling devices to loan to students and remain open for high needs students and those without alternative caregiving arrangements during HBL.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will continue to review the need for further periods of HBL, based on the prevailing COVID-19 situation and national posture.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The first one is: I understand the Minister's point about HBL not just for our Primary school students but also for keeping our PSLE cohort safe.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, moving forward beyond this week, does the Minister foresee the possibility of HBL being extended either into the future or perhaps even until the start of the school holidays?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Also bearing in mind that we have "N" Level, "O" Level and even "A" Level examinations coming up, does the Minister foresee the possibility to keep those cohorts, say, protected as well, that HBL might be rolled out in Secondary schools and beyond?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For Secondary schools and above, a vast majority of our students have already been vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The reason why I am not making the announcement today are as follows.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: One, we are in the middle of PSLE.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Second, we are also proceeding with our internal preparations and communications with our educators and I would like them to know our decision collectively first before we make the announcement in the latter part of this week, in tandem with the national posture.
